portal_hypertension.authors: Valentin S, Hlavaty A, Brossat C

portal_hypertension.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a rare and severe condition that may be associated with exposure to certain drugs. Bevacizumab, a monoclonal antibody targeting vascular endothelial growth factor, has been classified as having a possible association with PAH, but data remain scarce. This study aimed to assess the potential link between bevacizumab exposure and PAH through complementary clinical, medico-administrative and pharmacovigilance databases. We performed a multimodal investigation combining: 1) case identification from the French Pulmonary Hypertension (PH) Registry, 2) a population-based cohort analysis using the French National Health Data System (Système National des Donné...

portal_hypertension.abstract: Arterioportal (AP) shunts are a recognized vascular complication of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Severe AP shunts can cause portal hypertension, which can lead to complications such as variceal bleeding and refractory ascites. However, optimal management of HCC complicated by severe AP shunts remains challenging, particularly in patients with advanced disease. A 73-year-old woman presented with melena and massive hematemesis due to esophageal varices. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed multifocal HCC confined to the right hepatic lobe, Vp3 portal vein tumor thrombosis, and a high-flow AP shunt with hepatofugal portal flow.
